LESSON: THE CONSTITUTION OF KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 4.1: The Constitution of Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Constitution of Kenya, part of Political Developments and Governance in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need a constitution? 2. Why is integrity important in national leadership?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Constitution of Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Integrity: learners learn to choose to do the right time as they brainstorm on the guiding principles of leadership and integrity in

the Constitution of Kenya.

● Unity: learners exhibit cooperation and team spirit as they brainstorm in groups on the guiding principles of leadership and

integrity in the Constitution of Kenya.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Good governance: learners learn about guiding principles of leadership and integrity in the Constitution of Kenya when brainstorming

in groups.

● Social cohesion: learners work harmoniously when creating charts in groups showing the three arms of government, their roles and

interrelationships.

Link to other subjects:

● Kenyan Sign Language and English: learners apply the skill of effective communication as they debate on whether or not leaders

in Kenya adhere to their Constitutional responsibilities.

● Creative Arts and Sports: as learners create charts showing the three arms of government, their roles and interrelationships.
